candidate.title: TruSeq Nano
candidate.scope: The single TruSeq Nano product-preparation route in the assigned Illumina poster schematic, from double-stranded DNA through fragmentation/size selection, end repair/phosphorylation, A-overhang addition, indexed adaptor addition and ligation, and denaturation/amplification to a library ready for cluster generation. The biological target and insert substrate are DNA; downstream sequencing would interrogate the retained DNA insert sequence with physically linked index fields. This is a schematic architecture, not a complete experimental protocol or a claim about every TruSeq Nano kit version. The supplied card is secondary catalogue evidence and lists no primary publications; no publication date or historical origin is established.

operations.label: Fractionate / Size select
operations.description: Convert the long double-stranded DNA substrate into shorter fragments and retain a size-selected population, represented by the short staggered duplex.
operations.mechanism: Fragmentation and size selection are depicted as one combined stage; their execution is not resolved further.
operations.information_effect: The retained DNA fragments physically represent portions of the source DNA. Fragmentation changes their boundaries, and size selection limits which fragments proceed; the schematic does not establish complete or uniform representation of the starting DNA.

operations.label: End repair / Phosphorylate
operations.description: Normalize the offset fragment ends to blunt termini and introduce the terminal phosphate groups shown as P; repaired segments are colored purple.
operations.mechanism: End repair and phosphorylation as captioned; no enzyme identities or internal order are specified.
operations.information_effect: Prepare the DNA termini for subsequent modification while retaining the central insert.

operations.mechanism: Terminal A addition is shown; the P-marked opposite termini remain.
operations.information_effect: Changes the insert end structure while retaining the central DNA insert; index-bearing material is introduced at the next stage.

operations.mechanism: The ligation caption and joined product support covalent adaptor-to-insert joining. Compatibility of the A- and T-labeled tips is an interpretation of the depicted terminal bases.
operations.information_effect: Physically links the DNA insert to the adaptor regions labeled Index 1, Index 2, P5 and P7.

operations.label: Denature and amplify
operations.description: Process the forked adaptor-ligated DNA by the captioned denaturation and amplification stage, yielding the linear duplex library labeled ready for cluster generation.
operations.mechanism: Denaturation and amplification are grouped in the source; primers, enzymes and intermediate strand states are not shown.
operations.information_effect: The DNA insert is copied into an amplified library with physically linked Index 1 and Index 2 fields. Subsequent sequencing could identify the retained source-DNA fragment sequence and its attached indexes. The final P5/P7 labels and cluster-ready caption establish the depicted interface to cluster generation. No particular sample-to-index or cell association, sequence reads or quantitative recovery of original DNA molecules is established by this schematic.
